# Data Import & Preparation

## Data Preparation: All Eukaryotes
```{r Import QIIME2 Output}
# 1. Import QIIME 2 artifacts into a phyloseq object (feature table, tree, taxonomy, metadata)
ps <- qza_to_phyloseq(
  features = "Qiime2_output/table.qza", 
  tree     = "Qiime2_output/rooted-tree.qza", 
  taxonomy = "Qiime2_output/taxonomy.qza", 
  metadata = "Qiime2_output/metadata.txt"
)

# 2. Load representative ASV sequences from the QIIME 2 artifact
all_seqs <- read_qza("Qiime2_output/rep-seqs.qza")$data

# 3. Convert sequences to Biostrings DNAStringSet format for phyloseq compatibility
dna_seqs <- DNAStringSet(all_seqs)

# 4. Subset and align sequences to match active taxa names in the phyloseq object
dna_seqs_matched <- dna_seqs[taxa_names(ps)]

# 5. Merge representative sequences into the phyloseq object (populates the refseq slot)
ps <- merge_phyloseq(ps, dna_seqs_matched)
```

```{r Replace taxonomy with PR2 taxonomy}
# 1. Import raw tab-separated taxonomy output from QIIME 2
tax_raw <- read.delim("Qiime2_output/taxonomy.tsv", sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# 2. Parse PR2 taxonomy strings into 9 ranks, remove rank prefixes (e.g., 'g__'), trim whitespace, and set empty values to NA
tax_cleaned <- tax_raw %>%
  separate(
    Taxon, 
    into = c("Kingdom", "Supergroup", "Division", "Subdivision", 
             "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species"), 
    sep = ";", 
    fill = "right"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(Kingdom:Species, ~str_remove_all(., "^[[:lower:]]+_+"))) %>%
  mutate(across(Kingdom:Species, ~str_trim(.))) %>%
  mutate(across(Kingdom:Species, ~na_if(., "")))

# 3. Extract cleaned taxonomic ranks into a matrix format
tax_mat <- tax_cleaned %>%
  dplyr::select(Kingdom:Species) %>%
  as.matrix()

# 4. Assign ASV/Feature IDs as row names and attach cleaned taxonomy matrix to the phyloseq object
rownames(tax_mat) <- tax_cleaned$Feature.ID
tax_table(ps) <- tax_table(tax_mat)

# 5. Extract sample metadata from the phyloseq object into a standalone data frame
metadata <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))

# Extract total read counts per sample into a data frame
read_counts <- data.frame(
  SampleID = sample_names(ps),
  ReadCount = sample_sums(ps)
)
```

```{r Remove Controls}
# 1. Filter out control samples from the phyloseq object
ps_clean <- subset_samples(ps, type != "control")

# 2. Prune taxa with zero total abundance across remaining samples
ps_clean <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_clean) > 0, ps_clean)

# 3. Extract updated metadata for the cleaned sample dataset
metadata_clean <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_clean))
```

```{r Rarefy full phyloseq}
# Set seed for reproducible subsampling
set.seed(123)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Rarefaction Curve Generation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensure output directory exists
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Export rarefaction curve as high-resolution PNG
png("figures/Rarefaction_Curve.png", width = 2400, height = 1800, res = 300)

otu_tab_clean <- as(otu_table(ps_clean), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps_clean)) { otu_tab_clean <- t(otu_tab_clean) }

rarecurve(
  otu_tab_clean, 
  step = 50, 
  col = "blue", 
  label = FALSE, 
  main = "Rarefaction Curve",
  xlab = "Read Count",
  ylab = "No. ASVs",
  xlim = c(0, 10000)
)
abline(v = 8593, col = "red", lty = 2) # Threshold line for subsampling depth
dev.off()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Rarefy / Subsample Dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subsample phyloseq object to even depth (8,593 reads/sample) and remove orphaned taxa
ps_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(
  ps_clean, 
  sample.size = 8593, 
  replace = FALSE, 
  rngseed = 123
)
ps_rarefied <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_rarefied) > 0, ps_rarefied)
print(ps_rarefied)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Good's Coverage Calculation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Format OTU table for sample-wise coverage estimation [Coverage = 1 - (Singletons / Total Reads)]
otu_tab_rare <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps_rarefied))
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_rarefied)) { otu_tab_rare <- t(otu_tab_rare) }

goods_results <- apply(otu_tab_rare, 2, function(x) {
  x <- x[x > 0]
  1 - (sum(x == 1) / sum(x))
})

goods_df <- data.frame(
  SampleID = names(goods_results),
  GoodsCoverage = as.numeric(goods_results)
)

# Output summary metrics and evaluate against 95% threshold
cat("Average Good's Coverage:", round(mean(goods_df$GoodsCoverage), 4), "\n")
print(range(goods_df$GoodsCoverage))

if (all(goods_df$GoodsCoverage > 0.95)) {
  cat("Success: All samples have Good's Coverage > 0.95.\n")
} else {
  failed_samples <- goods_df[goods_df$GoodsCoverage <= 0.95, ]
  cat("Warning:", nrow(failed_samples), "samples failed the 0.95 threshold.\n")
  print(failed_samples)
}

# Export Good's coverage statistics to CSV files
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(goods_df, "statistics/Goods_Coverage.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Data Preparation: Algae only
```{r Create algae phyloseq}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define Taxonomic Inclusion & Exclusion Criteria
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
algae_include <- c("TSAR", "Archaeplastida", "Haptista", "Cryptista",
                   "Stramenopile", "Chlorophyta", "Bacillario", "Dinophyceae",
                   "Mediophyceae", "Coscinodiscophyceae", "Ochrophyta", "Skeletonema", 
                   "Thalassionema", "Thalassiosira")

algae_exclude <- c("Ciliophora", "Intramacronucleata", "Rhizaria", "Retaria",
                   "Metazoa", "Opisthokonta")

# Collapse vectors into unified regular expressions for fast vectorized matching
inc_pattern <- paste(algae_include, collapse = "|")
exc_pattern <- paste(algae_exclude, collapse = "|")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Extract Taxonomy & Concatenate Ranks
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
tax_df <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps_clean), "matrix"))
tax_strings <- apply(tax_df, 1, paste, collapse = " ")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Vectorized Taxa Filtering
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Match inclusion/exclusion patterns across full taxonomy strings
include_idx <- grepl(inc_pattern, tax_strings, ignore.case = TRUE)
exclude_idx <- grepl(exc_pattern, tax_strings, ignore.case = TRUE)

# Retain target algal taxa while strictly excluding non-algal/heterotrophic clades
final_algae_idx <- include_idx & !exclude_idx

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Subset Phyloseq Object & Prune Empty Features/Samples
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ps_algae <- prune_taxa(final_algae_idx, ps_clean) %>%
  prune_taxa(taxa_sums(.) > 0, .) %>%
  prune_samples(sample_sums(.) > 0, .)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Validation Check & Metadata Extraction
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verify zero excluded taxa remain in filtered dataset
check_strings <- apply(as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps_algae), "matrix")), 1, paste, collapse = " ")
n_bad_taxa <- sum(grepl(exc_pattern, check_strings, ignore.case = TRUE))
cat("Validation Check — Number of remaining excluded taxa:", n_bad_taxa, "\n")

# Extract sample metadata for the filtered algal phyloseq object
metadata_algae <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_algae))

read_counts <- data.frame(
  SampleID = sample_names(ps_algae),
  ReadCount = sample_sums(ps_algae)
)
```

```{r Rarefy algae phyloseq}
# Print summary metrics and evaluate against 0.95 quality threshold

print(range(goods_df$GoodsCoverage))

if (all(goods_df$GoodsCoverage > 0.95)) {
  cat("Success: All samples have Good's Coverage > 0.95.\n")
} else {
  failed_samples <- goods_df[goods_df$GoodsCoverage <= 0.95, ]
  cat("Warning:", nrow(failed_samples), "samples failed the 0.95 threshold.\n")
  print(failed_samples)
}

# Export results to CSV
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(goods_df, "statistics/Algae_Goods_Coverage.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Data Preparation: HAB taxa only
```{r Create HAB phyloseq}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define Target HAB (Harmful Algal Bloom) Taxa
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
hab_include <- c(
  "Alexandr", "Pseudo-nitz", "Pseudonitz", "Dinophysis", "Heterosigma", 
  "Margalefidinium", "Chaetoceros", "Phaeocystis", "Gonyaul", "Phaeocystal", 
  "Chaetocerotal", "Dinophysial", "Gymnodinial", "Peridinial", "Suessial"
)
hab_regex <- paste(hab_include, collapse = "|")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Identify and Subset HAB ASVs
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filter taxonomy matrix across all ranks for target HAB keywords
tax_df <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps_algae_rarefied), "matrix"))
hab_asvs <- tax_df %>%
  filter(if_any(everything(), ~ grepl(hab_regex, .x, ignore.case = TRUE))) %>%
  rownames()

# Subset rarefied phyloseq object to HAB taxa and remove zero-abundance samples
ps_HAB <- prune_taxa(hab_asvs, ps_algae_rarefied) %>%
  prune_samples(sample_sums(.) > 0, .)

metadata_HAB <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_HAB))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Relative Abundance Transformation & Sample Subsetting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Transform HAB counts to compositional relative abundance (0–1 scale)
ps_HAB_RelAbund <- transform_sample_counts(ps_HAB, function(x) x / sum(x))

# Subset HAB dataset to active environmental samples
ps_HAB_active <- subset_samples(ps_HAB, type == "active")
```

## Summary Statistics all Eukaryotes, algae & HAB taxa
```{r Summary Statistics}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Sequencing Depth Metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute summary statistics for sample read counts prior to rarefaction
read_depths <- sample_sums(ps_clean)
summary(read_depths)[c("Min.", "Mean", "Median", "Max.")]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Feature (ASV) Richness Summary
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract total ASV counts across full, algal, and HAB-filtered rarefied datasets
asv_counts <- c(
  all_asvs   = ntaxa(ps_rarefied),
  algae_asvs = ntaxa(ps_algae_rarefied),
  HAB_asvs   = ntaxa(ps_HAB)
)
print(asv_counts)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Taxonomic (Genus-Level) Richness Summary
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper function to count unique, non-NA genus assignments
count_unique_genera <- function(ps_obj) {
  length(na.omit(unique(as.character(tax_table(ps_obj)[, "Genus"]))))
}

# Calculate distinct genus counts across datasets
genus_counts <- c(
  all_genera   = count_unique_genera(ps_rarefied),
  algae_genera = count_unique_genera(ps_algae_rarefied),
  HAB_genera   = count_unique_genera(ps_HAB)
)
print(genus_counts)
```



##### Main Manuscript Figures #####
# Figure 1: Alpha Diversity
## Alpha Diversity Algae 
```{r Alpha Diversity Plot}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Calculate Alpha Diversity & Phylogenetic Diversity (Faith's PD)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Estimate standard alpha diversity metrics
richness_algae <- estimate_richness(
  ps_algae_rarefied, 
  measures = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "InvSimpson")
)

# Format OTU table for Faith's Phylogenetic Diversity calculation (samples as rows)
otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_algae_rarefied), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps_algae_rarefied)) {
  otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)
}

# Calculate Faith's PD using phyloseq phylogenetic tree
pd_out <- pd(otu_mat, phy_tree(ps_algae_rarefied), include.root = FALSE)

# Append Faith's PD and sample metadata to richness data frame
richness_algae$FaithsPD <- pd_out$PD
richness_algae <- cbind(richness_algae, sample_data(ps_algae_rarefied))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Data Reshaping & Factor Level Ordering
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Set chronological order for sampling months
richness_algae$month <- factor(
  richness_algae$month, 
  levels = c("March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October")
)

# Reshape data into long format for facet visualization
richness_long <- richness_algae %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "FaithsPD"), 
    names_to = "Metric", 
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# Set panel ordering for plot facets
richness_long$Metric <- factor(
  richness_long$Metric, 
  levels = c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "FaithsPD")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Visualization & File Export
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate faceted boxplot with jittered sample points
alpha_diversity_algae <- ggplot(richness_long, aes(x = month, y = Value, fill = type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_jitter(
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.8), 
    size = 1.2, 
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("active" = "#56B4E9", "passive" = "#E69F00")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position  = "bottom", 
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.title     = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Index Value", fill = "Sample Type") +
  ggtitle("Algae")

# Display plot
alpha_diversity_algae

# Export figure with directory verification
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave("figures/Algae_Alpha_Diversity_plot.png", alpha_diversity_algae, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r Alpha Diversity Statistics: Temporal}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data Subsetting & Variable Formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Convert metadata factors and subset dataset for targeted statistical comparisons
richness_algae$month <- as.factor(richness_algae$month)
richness_algae$replicate <- as.factor(richness_algae$replicate)

active_only <- subset(richness_algae, type == "active")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Non-Parametric Temporal Analysis Across Alpha Diversity Metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Define alpha diversity metrics to iterate through
indices <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "FaithsPD")

# Initialize output lists for test statistics
kw_list <- list()
dunn_list <- list()

# Run Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's post-hoc tests (BH p-adjust) across metrics
for (metric in indices) {
  
  formula_str <- as.formula(paste(metric, "~ month"))
  
  # 1. Kruskal-Wallis Test
  res_kw <- active_only %>% kruskal_test(formula_str)
  res_kw$Metric <- metric
  kw_list[[metric]] <- res_kw
  
  # 2. Dunn's Post-Hoc Test (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction)
  res_dunn <- active_only %>% dunn_test(formula_str, p.adjust.method = "BH")
  res_dunn$Metric <- metric
  dunn_list[[metric]] <- res_dunn
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Data Reorganization & Table Formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine results across metrics into single data frames
combined_kw <- do.call(rbind, kw_list)
combined_dunn <- do.call(rbind, dunn_list)

# Reorder columns to position Metric as the primary column
combined_kw <- combined_kw[, c("Metric", setdiff(names(combined_kw), "Metric"))]
combined_dunn <- combined_dunn[, c("Metric", setdiff(names(combined_dunn), "Metric"))]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Export Statistical Tables
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

write.csv(combined_kw, "statistics/Algae_Alpha_Diversity_Temporal_KW.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(combined_dunn, "statistics/Algae_Alpha_Diversity_Temporal_Dunn.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r Alpha Diversity Statistics: Sampling Method}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Subset Data & Create Interaction Factor (Active vs. Passive in July & August)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subset dataset to include only July and August samples
july_august <- subset(richness_algae, month %in% c("July", "August"))

# Combine sample type and month into a unified interaction factor for group-wise comparisons
july_august$group <- factor(paste(july_august$type, july_august$month, sep = "_"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Non-Parametric Group Analysis Across Alpha Diversity Metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Define diversity metrics to iterate through
indices <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "FaithsPD")

# Initialize output lists for test statistics
kw_list <- list()
dunn_list <- list()

# Run Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's post-hoc tests (BH p-adjust) across metrics
for (metric in indices) {
  
  formula_str <- as.formula(paste(metric, "~ group"))
  
  # 1. Kruskal-Wallis Test
  res_kw <- july_august %>% kruskal_test(formula_str)
  res_kw$Metric <- metric
  kw_list[[metric]] <- res_kw
  
  # 2. Dunn's Post-Hoc Test (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction)
  res_dunn <- july_august %>% dunn_test(formula_str, p.adjust.method = "BH")
  res_dunn$Metric <- metric
  dunn_list[[metric]] <- res_dunn
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Data Reorganization & Table Formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine results across metrics into single data frames
combined_kw <- do.call(rbind, kw_list)
combined_dunn <- do.call(rbind, dunn_list)

# Reorder columns to position Metric as the primary column
combined_kw <- combined_kw[, c("Metric", setdiff(names(combined_kw), "Metric"))]
combined_dunn <- combined_dunn[, c("Metric", setdiff(names(combined_dunn), "Metric"))]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Export Statistical Tables
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

write.csv(combined_kw, "statistics/Algae_Alpha_Diversity_Method_KW.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(combined_dunn, "statistics/Algae_Alpha_Diversity_Method_Dunn.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r Alpha Diversity Statistics: Temporal Dynamics}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data Subsetting & Variable Formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Convert metadata factors and subset dataset for targeted statistical comparisons
richness_HAB$month <- as.factor(richness_HAB$month)
richness_HAB$replicate <- as.factor(richness_HAB$replicate)

active_only <- subset(richness_HAB, type == "active")
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Non-Parametric Temporal Analysis Across Alpha Diversity Metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Define alpha diversity metrics to iterate through
indices <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "FaithsPD")

# Initialize output lists for test statistics
kw_list <- list()
dunn_list <- list()

# Run Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's post-hoc tests (BH p-adjust) across metrics
for (metric in indices) {
  
  formula_str <- as.formula(paste(metric, "~ month"))
  
  # 1. Kruskal-Wallis Test
  res_kw <- active_only %>% kruskal_test(formula_str)
  res_kw$Metric <- metric
  kw_list[[metric]] <- res_kw
  
  # 2. Dunn's Post-Hoc Test (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction)
  res_dunn <- active_only %>% dunn_test(formula_str, p.adjust.method = "BH")
  res_dunn$Metric <- metric
  dunn_list[[metric]] <- res_dunn
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Data Reorganization & Table Formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine results across metrics into single data frames
combined_kw <- do.call(rbind, kw_list)
combined_dunn <- do.call(rbind, dunn_list)

# Reorder columns to position Metric as the primary column
combined_kw <- combined_kw[, c("Metric", setdiff(names(combined_kw), "Metric"))]
combined_dunn <- combined_dunn[, c("Metric", setdiff(names(combined_dunn), "Metric"))]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Export Statistical Tables
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

write.csv(combined_kw, "statistics/HAB_Alpha_Diversity_Temporal_KW.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(combined_dunn, "statistics/HAB_Alpha_Diversity_Temporal_Dunn.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Table 1A: Kruskal-Wallis: Temporal
```{r Algae & HAB Taxa: Temporal}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define Phyloseq Target List & Diversity Metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Map dataset subsets to descriptive names for manuscript publication
# (Add "All Eukaryotes" = ps_rarefied here if you want the full clean dataset included)
ps_list <- list(
  "Algal Taxa" = ps_algae_rarefied,
  "HAB Taxa"   = ps_HAB
)

indices <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "FaithsPD")
all_subsets_list <- list()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Iterate Across Datasets & Compute Temporal Non-Parametric Statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
for (sub_name in names(ps_list)) {
  ps_sub <- ps_list[[sub_name]]
  
  # Calculate standard alpha diversity indices
  alpha_df <- estimate_richness(ps_sub, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson"))
  
  # Calculate Faith's PD if phylogenetic tree exists, else assign NA
  if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_sub, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
    otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_sub), "matrix")
    if (taxa_are_rows(ps_sub)) { otu_mat <- t(otu_mat) }
    pd_res <- pd(otu_mat, phy_tree(ps_sub), include.root = FALSE)
    alpha_df$FaithsPD <- pd_res$PD
  } else {
    alpha_df$FaithsPD <- NA
  }
  
  # Merge metadata with calculated alpha diversity metrics
  df_combined <- cbind(data.frame(sample_data(ps_sub)), alpha_df)
  
  # Run Kruskal-Wallis test across sampling months for each metric
  kw_metrics <- list()
  for (metric in indices) {
    if (all(is.na(df_combined[[metric]]))) next
    
    res <- df_combined %>%
      kruskal_test(as.formula(paste(metric, "~ month"))) %>%
      mutate(Metric = metric) %>%
      select(Metric, n, df, statistic, p)
    
    kw_metrics[[metric]] <- res
  }
  
  # Combine metric results and pivot into wide format per subset
  wide_kw <- bind_rows(kw_metrics) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      id_cols = c(n, df),
      names_from = Metric,
      values_from = c(statistic, p),
      names_glue = "{Metric}_{.value}"
    ) %>%
    mutate(Subset = sub_name)
  
  # Ensure target columns exist even if FaithsPD was skipped
  for (m in indices) {
    if (!paste0(m, "_statistic") %in% names(wide_kw)) wide_kw[[paste0(m, "_statistic")]] <- NA_real_
    if (!paste0(m, "_p") %in% names(wide_kw)) wide_kw[[paste0(m, "_p")]] <- NA_real_
  }
  
  all_subsets_list[[sub_name]] <- wide_kw
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Format & Export Final Manuscript Table (Table 1A)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine subsets and reorder columns for publication layout
final_kw_table <- bind_rows(all_subsets_list) %>%
  select(
    Subset,
    N = n,
    df,
    `Observed H`          = Observed_statistic,
    `Observed p`          = Observed_p,
    `Shannon H`           = Shannon_statistic,
    `Shannon p`           = Shannon_p,
    `Inverse Simpson H`   = InvSimpson_statistic,
    `Inverse Simpson p`   = InvSimpson_p,
    `Faith's PD H`        = FaithsPD_statistic,
    `Faith's PD p`        = FaithsPD_p
  )

# Display summary table in console
print(final_kw_table)

# Export statistical summary to CSV
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(
  final_kw_table, 
  "statistics/Table_1A.csv", 
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Table 1B: Significant Dunn's test: Temporal
```{r Algae & HAB Taxa: Temporal}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define Phyloseq Target List & Diversity Metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Map dataset subsets to descriptive names for manuscript publication
ps_list <- list(
  "Algal Taxa" = ps_algae_rarefied,
  "HAB"        = ps_HAB
)

indices <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "FaithsPD")
all_subsets_list <- list()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Iterate Across Datasets & Compute Pairwise Dunn's Post-Hoc Tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
for (sub_name in names(ps_list)) {
  # Use ps_sub to avoid overwriting global raw unrarefied ps object
  ps_sub <- ps_list[[sub_name]]
  
  # Calculate standard alpha diversity indices
  alpha_df <- estimate_richness(ps_sub, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson"))
  
  # Calculate Faith's PD if phylogenetic tree exists, else assign NA
  if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_sub, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
    otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_sub), "matrix")
    if (taxa_are_rows(ps_sub)) { otu_mat <- t(otu_mat) }
    pd_res <- pd(otu_mat, phy_tree(ps_sub), include.root = FALSE)
    alpha_df$FaithsPD <- pd_res$PD
  } else {
    alpha_df$FaithsPD <- NA
  }
  
  # Merge metadata with calculated alpha diversity metrics
  df_combined <- cbind(data.frame(sample_data(ps_sub)), alpha_df)
  
  # Run Dunn's test (BH p-value adjustment) across months for each metric
  dunn_metrics <- list()
  for (metric in indices) {
    if (all(is.na(df_combined[[metric]]))) next
    
    res <- df_combined %>%
      dunn_test(as.formula(paste(metric, "~ month")), p.adjust.method = "BH") %>%
      mutate(
        Contrast = paste(group1, "vs", group2),
        Metric   = metric
      ) %>%
      select(Contrast, Metric, statistic, p.adj)
    
    dunn_metrics[[metric]] <- res
  }
  
  # Combine metric results and pivot into wide format per subset
  wide_dunn <- bind_rows(dunn_metrics) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from  = Metric,
      values_from = c(statistic, p.adj),
      names_glue  = "{Metric}_{.value}"
    )
  
  # Ensure target columns exist even if FaithsPD was skipped
  for (m in indices) {
    if (!paste0(m, "_statistic") %in% names(wide_dunn)) wide_dunn[[paste0(m, "_statistic")]] <- NA
    if (!paste0(m, "_p.adj") %in% names(wide_dunn)) wide_dunn[[paste0(m, "_p.adj")]] <- NA
  }
  
  # Filter contrasts where at least one metric is statistically significant (p.adj < 0.05)
  sig_dunn <- wide_dunn %>%
    filter(
      (Observed_p.adj < 0.05 & !is.na(Observed_p.adj)) | 
      (Shannon_p.adj < 0.05 & !is.na(Shannon_p.adj)) | 
      (InvSimpson_p.adj < 0.05 & !is.na(InvSimpson_p.adj)) | 
      (FaithsPD_p.adj < 0.05 & !is.na(FaithsPD_p.adj))
    ) %>%
    mutate(Subset = sub_name)
  
  all_subsets_list[[sub_name]] <- sig_dunn
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Format & Export Final Manuscript Table (Table 1B)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine subsets and reorder columns for publication layout
final_dunn_table <- bind_rows(all_subsets_list) %>%
  select(
    Subset,
    Contrast,
    `Observed estimate`          = Observed_statistic,
    `Observed Adjusted p`        = Observed_p.adj,
    `Shannon estimate`           = Shannon_statistic,
    `Shannon Adjusted p`         = Shannon_p.adj,
    `Inverse Simpson estimate`   = InvSimpson_statistic,
    `Inverse Simpson Adjusted p` = InvSimpson_p.adj,
    `Faith's PD estimate`        = FaithsPD_statistic,
    `Faith's PD Adjusted p`      = FaithsPD_p.adj
  )

# Inspect head of summary table
head(final_dunn_table)

# Export statistical summary to CSV
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(
  final_dunn_table, 
  "statistics/Table_1B.csv", 
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Table S2: Kruskal-Wallis: Sampling Method
```{r Algae & HAB Taxa: Sampling Method}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define Phyloseq Target List & Diversity Metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Map dataset subsets to descriptive names for manuscript publication
ps_list <- list(
  "Algal Taxa" = ps_algae_rarefied,
  "HAB Taxa"   = ps_HAB
)

indices <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "FaithsPD")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Iterate Across Subsets & Test Sampling Method Differences (July & August)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute Kruskal-Wallis tests comparing sampling types (active vs. passive) in July & August
raw_kw_sampling <- map_dfr(names(ps_list), function(sub_name) {
  
  # Subset to peak bloom months (July/August) and assign to ps_sub to protect workspace
  ps_sub <- subset_samples(ps_list[[sub_name]], month %in% c("July", "August"))
  
  # Calculate standard alpha diversity metrics
  alpha <- estimate_richness(ps_sub, measures = indices[1:3])
  
  # Calculate Faith's PD if phylogenetic tree exists, else assign NA
  if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_sub, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
    otu <- as(otu_table(ps_sub), "matrix")
    if (taxa_are_rows(ps_sub)) otu <- t(otu)
    alpha$FaithsPD <- pd(otu, phy_tree(ps_sub), include.root = FALSE)$PD
  } else { 
    alpha$FaithsPD <- NA 
  }
  
  # Combine metadata, reshape to long format, and execute group-wise Kruskal-Wallis tests
  cbind(data.frame(sample_data(ps_sub)), alpha) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = any_of(indices), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Val") %>%
    drop_na(Val) %>%
    group_by(Metric) %>%
    kruskal_test(Val ~ type) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      id_cols     = c(n, df), 
      names_from  = Metric, 
      values_from = c(statistic, p), 
      names_glue  = "{Metric}_{.value}"
    ) %>%
    mutate(Subset = sub_name, .before = 1)
})

# Ensure all expected metric columns exist even if FaithsPD was skipped
for (m in indices) {
  if (!paste0(m, "_statistic") %in% names(raw_kw_sampling)) raw_kw_sampling[[paste0(m, "_statistic")]] <- NA_real_
  if (!paste0(m, "_p") %in% names(raw_kw_sampling)) raw_kw_sampling[[paste0(m, "_p")]] <- NA_real_
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Format & Export Final Manuscript Table (Table S2A)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Select and rename columns for publication layout
final_kw_sampling_table <- raw_kw_sampling %>%
  select(
    Subset,
    N = n,
    df,
    `Observed H`          = Observed_statistic,
    `Observed p`          = Observed_p,
    `Shannon H`           = Shannon_statistic,
    `Shannon p`           = Shannon_p,
    `Inverse Simpson H`   = InvSimpson_statistic,
    `Inverse Simpson p`   = InvSimpson_p,
    `Faith's PD H`        = FaithsPD_statistic,
    `Faith's PD p`        = FaithsPD_p
  )

# Display formatted table in console
print(final_kw_sampling_table)

# Export to statistics directory
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(final_kw_sampling_table, "statistics/Table_S2A.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r Algae: NMDS Plot}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Temporal Metadata Formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Order sampling months chronologically for consistent plot legend ordering
sample_data(ps_algae_rarefied)$month <- factor(
  sample_data(ps_algae_rarefied)$month, 
  levels = c("March", "April", "May", "June", 
             "July", "August", "September", "October")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Compute Non-Metric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate Bray-Curtis distance matrix and run NMDS ordination
nmds_ord_algae <- ordinate(ps_algae_rarefied, method = "NMDS", distance = "bray")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Construct Ordination Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract baseline ordination coordinates and clear default phyloseq layers
# 1. Ensure month factor levels are ordered
ps_algae_rarefied@sam_data$month <- factor(
  ps_algae_rarefied@sam_data$month,
  levels = c("March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October"),
  ordered = TRUE
)

# 2. Re-spaced 8-step Blue Scale (Optimized for equal perceived steps)
blue_hues <- c(
  "March"     = "#EFF3FF",  # Very light ice blue
  "April"     = "#C6DBEF",  # Soft sky blue
  "May"       = "#9ECAE1",  # Light blue
  "June"      = "#6BAED6",  # Medium blue
  "July"      = "#4292C6",  # Deep cerulean
  "August"    = "#2171B5",  # Royal blue
  "September" = "#08519C",  # Navy blue
  "October"   = "#081D58"   # Dark indigo-navy (lightened enough to read)
)

# 3. Build plot with subtle outline for clarity
nmds_algae <- plot_ordination(ps_algae_rarefied, nmds_ord, type = "samples")
nmds_algae$layers <- NULL

nmds_algae <- nmds_algae + 
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = month, shape = type), 
    size = 3.8,      
    stroke = 0.5,  
    color = "grey20"  # Dark grey outline instead of pure black
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("active" = 21, "passive" = 24)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = blue_hues) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, stroke = 0.5, color = "grey20")),
    shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      fill = "white", 
      color = "grey20",
      stroke = 0.5 
    ))
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    legend.title     = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 11),
    text             = element_text(color = "black")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Algae", 
    fill  = "Sampling Month", 
    shape = "Sample Type"
  ) +
  force_panelsizes(
    rows = unit(4, "in"), 
    cols = unit(4, "in")
  )

print(nmds_algae)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Export Figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggsave("Analysis/Figures/All/Figure_2A.png", nmds_algae, height = 5, width = 6, dpi = 300)


# 5. Stress

print(nmds_ord_algae$stress)
```

```{r Statistics Algae: Permanova}
# Ensure output directory exists
dir.create("statistics", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. TEMPORAL ANALYSIS (Active Sampling Only)
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.1 Data Preparation & Distance Matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subset dataset to active sampling methods across all months
ps_algae_active   <- subset_samples(ps_algae_rarefied, type == "active")
dist_algae_active <- phyloseq::distance(ps_algae_active, method = "bray")
meta_algae_active <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_algae_active))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.2 Temporal PERMANOVA
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
permanova_algae_month <- adonis2(dist_algae_active ~ month, data = meta_algae_active)
print(permanova_algae_month)

sink("statistics/Algae_permanova_temporal.txt")
print(permanova_algae_month)
sink()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.3 NMDS Ordination Stress Evaluation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
nmds_nmds_ord_algae <- metaMDS(dist_algae_active, k = 2, trymax = 100)
cat("NMDS Stress Value: ", nmds_ord_algae$stress, "\n")

sink("statistics/Algae_NMDS_Stress.txt")
cat("NMDS Stress Value: ", nmds_ord_algae$stress, "\n")
sink()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.4 Temporal Homogeneity of Multivariate Dispersions (PERMDISP)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
disper_algae_month <- betadisper(dist_algae_active, group = meta_algae_active$month)

set.seed(123)
disper_algae_month_test <- permutest(disper_algae_month, permutations = 999)
print(disper_algae_month_test)

sink("statistics/Algae_betadisper_temporal.txt")
print(disper_algae_month)
print(disper_algae_month_test)
sink()


# ==============================================================================
# 2. METHODOLOGICAL ANALYSIS (July & August Only: Active vs. Passive)

  by = "terms"
)

sink()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

sink("statistics/Algae_betadisper_method.txt")
```

```{r HAB taxa: NMDS Plot}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```{r Statistics HAB: Permanova}
permanova_HAB_month <- adonis2(dist_HAB_active ~ month, data = meta_HAB_active)
print(permanova_HAB_month)

sink("statistics/HAB_permanova_temporal.txt")
print(permanova_HAB_month)
sink()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.3 NMDS Ordination Stress Evaluation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
nmds_nmds_ord_HAB <- metaMDS(dist_HAB_active, k = 2, trymax = 100)
cat("NMDS Stress Value: ", nmds_ord_HAB$stress, "\n")

sink("statistics/HAB_NMDS_Stress.txt")
cat("NMDS Stress Value: ", nmds_ord_HAB$stress, "\n")
sink()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.4 Temporal Homogeneity of Multivariate Dispersions (PERMDISP)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
disper_HAB_month <- betadisper(dist_HAB_active, group = meta_HAB_active$month)

disper_HAB_month_test <- permutest(disper_HAB_month, permutations = 999)
print(disper_HAB_month_test)

sink("statistics/HAB_betadisper_temporal.txt")
print(disper_HAB_month)
print(disper_HAB_month_test)
sink()

# ==============================================================================
# 2. METHODOLOGICAL ANALYSIS (July & August Only: Active vs. Passive)
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.1 Data Preparation & Distance Matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subset dataset to peak bloom months comparing sampling methods
ps_HAB_type   <- subset_samples(ps_HAB_rarefied, month %in% c("July", "August"))
dist_HAB_type <- phyloseq::distance(ps_HAB_type, method = "bray")
meta_HAB_type <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_HAB_type))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.2 Factorial PERMANOVA (Method x Month Interaction)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

permanova_HAB_type <- adonis2(
  dist_HAB_type ~ type * month, 
  data = meta_HAB_type, 
  by = "terms"
)
print(permanova_HAB_type)

sink("statistics/HAB_permanova_method.txt")
print(permanova_HAB_type)
sink()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.3 Sampling Method Homogeneity of Multivariate Dispersions (PERMDISP)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
disper_HAB_type <- betadisper(dist_HAB_type, group = meta_HAB_type$type)

disper_HAB_type_test <- permutest(disper_HAB_type, permutations = 999)
print(disper_HAB_type_test)

sink("statistics/HAB_betadisper_method.txt")
print(disper_HAB_type)
print(disper_HAB_type_test)
sink()
```

```{r 3A Algae: Class-level Relative Abundance Plot}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Color Palette & Abundance Threshold Definition
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strict colorblind-friendly palette (Okabe-Ito / Tol qualitative mix)
algae_colors <- c(
  "Other"             = "#888888", # Neutral Grey
  "Cryptophyceae"     = "#56B4E9", # Sky Blue
  "Dinophyceae"       = "#E69F00", # Warm Amber / Gold
  "Mamiellophyceae"   = "#009E73", # Teal Green
  "Mediophyceae"      = "#0072B2", # Strong Blue
  "Prymnesiophyceae"  = "#D55E00", # Vermilion / Rust
  "Syndiniales"       = "#CC79A7", # Reddish Purple / Magenta
  "Ulvophyceae"       = "#F0E442", # Bright Yellow
  "Bacillariophyceae" = "#661100", # Dark Chestnut Brown
  "Chrysophyceae"     = "#AA4499", # Bright Purple
  "Picomonadea"       = "#66CCEE", # High-contrast Ice Blue
  "Picozoa_XX"        = "#332299", # Deep Navy
  "Telonemia_XX"      = "#DDCC77"  # Pale Sand / Ochre
)

# Relative abundance filtering threshold (2%)
threshold <- 0.02  

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Phyloseq Processing & Taxonomic Agglomeration
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filter metadata for active sampling methods only
ps_algae_active <- subset_samples(ps_algae_rarefied, type == "active")

# Convert raw rarefied counts to relative abundance (0–1 scale)
ps_rel_algae <- transform_sample_counts(ps_algae_active, function(x) x / sum(x))

# Agglomerate relative abundances to Class level
ps_class_algae <- tax_glom(ps_rel_algae, taxrank = "Class", NArm = FALSE)

# Melt phyloseq object to long data frame for ggplot formatting
df_long_algae <- psmelt(ps_class_algae)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Community Relative Abundance Summarization & Low-Abundance Collapsing
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_data_algae <- df_long_algae %>%
  mutate(
    Class = case_when(
      is.na(Class) | str_trim(Class) %in% c("", "NA") ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ Class
    )
  ) %>%
  # Calculate monthly mean relative abundance per Class
  group_by(month, Class) %>%
  summarise(mean_rel_abund = mean(Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Re-normalize to ensure 100% per month
  group_by(month) %>%
  mutate(mean_rel_abund = mean_rel_abund / sum(mean_rel_abund)) %>%
  # Collapse classes below the threshold into "Other"
  mutate(
    Class_collapsed = if_else(mean_rel_abund < threshold, "Other", Class)
  ) %>%
  # Re-aggregate collapsed classes
  group_by(month, Class_collapsed) %>%
  summarise(mean_rel_abund = sum(mean_rel_abund), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Order months chronologically
  mutate(
    month = factor(month, levels = c("March", "April", "May", "June", 
                                     "July", "August", "September", "October"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(month))

# Set factor levels to place "Other" first in legend ordering
unique_classes_algae <- sort(unique(plot_data_algae$Class_collapsed))
legend_order_algae   <- c("Other", setdiff(unique_classes_algae, "Other"))

write.csv(plot_data_algae,"Manuscript/Tables/Algae_Rel_Abund_Class.csv")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Construct Stacked Relative Abundance Bar Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
algae_Class <- ggplot(
  plot_data_algae, 
  aes(x = month, y = mean_rel_abund, fill = factor(Class_collapsed, levels = legend_order_algae))
) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = FALSE), width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = algae_colors, name = "Class") +
  labs(
    x     = "Sampling Month",
    y     = "Relative Abundance",
    title = "A) Algal Taxa"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    text         = element_text(color = "black"),
    plot.title   = element_text(color = "black", size = 13, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
    axis.title.y = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black", size = 11),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(color = "black", size = 11),
    legend.title = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.text  = element_text(color = "black", size = 11),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8)
  ) +
  force_panelsizes(rows = unit(3, "in"), cols = unit(4, "in"))

# Display plot in console
print(algae_Class)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Export Figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave("figures/Figure_3A.png", algae_Class, height = 5, width = 7, dpi = 300)
```
```{r 3B HAB Taxa: Genus-level Relative Abundance Plot}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Setup & Abundance Threshold Definition
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Relative abundance filtering threshold (2%)
threshold <- 0.02 

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Phyloseq Processing & Taxonomic Agglomeration
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subset dataset to active sampling methods only
ps_HAB_active <- subset_samples(ps_HAB, type == "active")

# Convert raw rarefied counts to relative abundance (0–1 scale)
ps_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_HAB_active, function(x) x / sum(x))

# Agglomerate relative abundances to Genus level
ps_Genus <- tax_glom(ps_rel, taxrank = "Genus", NArm = FALSE)

# Melt phyloseq object to long data frame for ggplot formatting
df_long <- psmelt(ps_Genus)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Community Relative Abundance Summarization & Low-Abundance Collapsing
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_data_HAB <- df_long %>%
  mutate(
    Genus = case_when(
      is.na(Genus) | str_trim(Genus) %in% c("", "NA") ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ Genus
    )
  ) %>%
  # Calculate monthly mean relative abundance per Genus
  group_by(month, Genus) %>%
  summarise(mean_rel_abund = mean(Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Re-normalize to ensure 100% per month
  group_by(month) %>%
  mutate(mean_rel_abund = mean_rel_abund / sum(mean_rel_abund)) %>%
  # Collapse genera below threshold into "Other"
  mutate(
    Genus_collapsed = if_else(mean_rel_abund < threshold, "Other", Genus)
  ) %>%
  # Re-aggregate collapsed genera
  group_by(month, Genus_collapsed) %>%
  summarise(mean_rel_abund = sum(mean_rel_abund), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Order months chronologically
  mutate(
    month = factor(month, levels = c("March", "April", "May", "June", 
                                     "July", "August", "September", "October"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(month))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Colorblind-Friendly Palette & Legend Label Formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
unique_Genus <- sort(unique(plot_data_HAB$Genus_collapsed))

# Position "Other" at the base of the stack and top of legend
legend_order <- c("Other", setdiff(unique_Genus, "Other"))
num_genera   <- length(setdiff(legend_order, "Other"))

# Extended Paul Tol Qualitative Palette (Bright + Vibrant)
tol_qualitative <- c("#EE6677", "#4477AA", "#CCBB44", "#228833", 
                     "#AA3377", "#66CCEE", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#56B4E9")

# Expand palette dynamically if distinct genera exceed palette length
if (num_genera <= length(tol_qualitative)) {
  base_colors <- tol_qualitative[1:num_genera]
} else {
  base_colors <- colorRampPalette(tol_qualitative)(num_genera)
}

# Shuffle colors to maximize visual separation between adjacent stacked bars
set.seed(42) # Ensure reproducible color assignment across re-runs
shuffled_colors <- sample(base_colors)

# Map neutral dark grey to "Other" and shuffled colors to genera
my_colors <- setNames(c("#777777", shuffled_colors), legend_order)

# Format legend labels: plain text for "Other", italicized for taxonomic genus names
legend_labels <- parse(text = ifelse(legend_order == "Other", "'Other'", paste0("italic('", legend_order, "')")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Construct Stacked Relative Abundance Bar Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
HAB_Genus <- ggplot(
  plot_data_HAB, 
  aes(x = month, y = mean_rel_abund, fill = factor(Genus_collapsed, levels = legend_order))
) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = FALSE), width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors, name = "Genus", labels = legend_labels) +
  labs(
    x     = "Sampling Month",
    y     = "Relative Abundance",
    title = "B) Genera containing HAB species"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(color = "black"),
    plot.title       = element_text(color = "black", size = 13, face = "bold"),
    strip.text       = element_text(color = "black", size = 13, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    strip.background = element_blank(), 
    axis.title.x     = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
    axis.title.y     = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black", size = 11),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(color = "black", size = 11),
    legend.title     = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.text      = element_text(color = "black", size = 11),
    panel.border     = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8)
  ) +
  force_panelsizes(rows = unit(3, "in"), cols = unit(4, "in"))

# Display plot in console
print(HAB_Genus)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Export Figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave("figures/Figure_3B.png", HAB_Genus, height = 5, width = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# Figure 4: HAB Seasonal Dynamics
```{r Pseudo-nitzschia species(complex) line plot}
# Ensure output directory exists for exported figures
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. SEQUENCE ALIGNMENT & TAXONOMIC MATCHING (PR2 DATABASE)
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.1 Subset Pseudo-nitzschia ASVs and Reference Data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract Pseudo-nitzschia ASVs, reference sequences, and total read counts
ps_pn     <- subset_taxa(ps_algae, Genus == "Pseudo-nitzschia")
asv_seqs  <- refseq(ps_pn)
asv_reads <- taxa_sums(ps_pn)

# Load PR2 reference database and filter for Pseudo-nitzschia reference entries
pr2    <- readDNAStringSet("pr2_v5.1.1_SSU_dada2.fasta.gz")
pr2_pn <- pr2[str_detect(names(pr2), "Pseudo-nitzschia")]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.2 Pairwise Alignment against PR2 Reference Database
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Align each ASV to PR2 entries to calculate percent identity and extract top matches
pn_aligned <- map_dfr(names(asv_seqs), function(id) {
  # Perform global-local pairwise alignment and calculate percent identity (PID1)
  pids    <- pid(pairwiseAlignment(pr2_pn, asv_seqs[[id]], type = "global-local"), type = "PID1")
  max_pid <- max(pids)
  
  # Extract top-matching reference headers at maximum identity
  top_headers   <- names(pr2_pn)[pids == max_pid]
  clean_headers <- gsub(";\\s*$", "", top_headers)
  top_species   <- unique(str_replace_all(sub(".*[;|]", "", clean_headers), "_", " "))
  
  data.frame(
    OTU             = id,
    `Read number`   = asv_reads[[id]],
    Pct_Identity    = round(max_pid, 2),
    `Top PR2 Match` = paste(top_species[top_species != ""], collapse = " / "),
    check.names     = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.3 Filter & Summarize Species Complexes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filter for 100% identity matches and minimum read count threshold (>= 10 reads)
pn_complex_summary <- pn_aligned %>%
  filter(Pct_Identity == 100, `Read number` >= 10) %>%
  mutate(
    `Species (complex)` = case_when(
      grepl("pungens", `Top PR2 Match`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "P. pungens",
      grepl("delicatissima|pseudodelicatissima", `Top PR2 Match`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "P. delicatissima complex",
      grepl("australis|seriata", `Top PR2 Match`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "P. seriata complex",
      TRUE ~ "Pseudo-nitzschia sp."
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(`Species (complex)`, `Top PR2 Match`) %>%
  summarise(
    `Read number` = sum(`Read number`),
    .groups       = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(`Read number`))

# Print summary table to console
print(pn_complex_summary)


# ==============================================================================
# 2. SEASONAL RELATIVE ABUNDANCE ANALYSIS & PLOTTING
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.1 Map High-Confidence Categories & Merge with Community Profiles
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Map OTUs with 100% PR2 identity and >= 10 reads to their assigned match category
asv_categories <- pn_aligned %>%
  filter(Pct_Identity == 100, `Read number` >= 10) %>%
  mutate(Category = `Top PR2 Match`) %>%
  dplyr::select(OTU, Category)

# Convert community counts to relative abundance (%) and join category mappings
ps_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_algae, function(x) x / sum(x) * 100)

pn_data <- psmelt(ps_rel) %>%
  inner_join(asv_categories, by = "OTU") %>%
  group_by(Sample, month, Category) %>%
  summarize(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.2 Rank & Filter Taxa Categories
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Retain categories with overall mean abundance >= 0.01% and rank by mean abundance
category_order <- pn_data %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  summarize(Overall_Mean = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(Overall_Mean >= 0.01) %>%
  arrange(desc(Overall_Mean)) %>%
  pull(Category)

month_order <- c("March", "April", "May", "June", 
                 "July", "August", "September", "October")

# Summarize monthly mean relative abundance and standard error (SE)
plot_data_pn <- pn_data %>%
  filter(Category %in% category_order) %>%
  group_by(month, Category) %>%
  summarize(
    Mean_Abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE             = sd(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups        = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    month    = factor(month, levels = month_order),
    Category = factor(Category, levels = category_order) # Controls legend ordering
  )

#write.csv(plot_data_pn,"Analysis/Tables/all/Pseudo-nitzschia_RelAbund.csv")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.3 Aesthetic Styling & Markdown Legend Formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Format legend labels using Markdown syntax for selective taxonomic italicization
legend_labels <- category_order %>%
  str_replace_all("\\bPseudo-nitzschia\\b", "*Pseudo-nitzschia*") %>%
  str_replace_all("\\bP\\.", "*P.*") %>%
  str_replace_all("\\b([a-z]{3,})\\b", "*\\1*") %>%
  str_replace_all("\\*sp\\*\\.", "sp.") %>%
  str_replace_all("\\*sp\\*", "sp") %>%
  str_replace_all("\\*complex\\*", "complex") %>%
  str_replace_all("\\* \\*", " ")

n_cats <- length(category_order)

# Subset palettes dynamically to match category count
orange_palette <- c("#541500", "#8C2D04", "#F16913", "#FDAE6B", "#E6550D", "#A63603")[1:n_cats]
shape_palette  <- c(16, 17, 15, 18, 25, 19, 8)[1:n_cats]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.4 Construct Seasonal Dynamics Line Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Pseudonitzschia_seasonal <- ggplot(
  plot_data_pn, 
  aes(x = month, y = Mean_Abundance, group = Category, color = Category, fill = Category, shape = Category)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = pmax(0, Mean_Abundance - SE), ymax = Mean_Abundance + SE), 
    alpha = 0.20, 
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = orange_palette, labels = legend_labels) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = orange_palette, labels = legend_labels) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shape_palette, labels = legend_labels) +
  labs(
    x = "Sampling Month",
    y = "Relative Abundance (%)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position  = "right",
    legend.text      = ggtext::element_markdown(), # Renders Markdown italics in legend
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    legend.title     = element_blank()
  ) +
  force_panelsizes(
    rows = unit(2, "in"), 
    cols = unit(4, "in")
  )

# Display plot in console
print(Pseudonitzschia_seasonal)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.5 Export Figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggsave("figures/Figure_4_Pseudonitzschia.png", Pseudonitzschia_seasonal, width = 10, height = 3, dpi = 300)
```

```{r Alexandrium species(complex) line plot}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. SEQUENCE ALIGNMENT & TAXONOMIC MATCHING (PR2 DATABASE)
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.1 Subset Alexandrium ASVs and Reference Data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract Alexandrium ASVs, reference sequences, and total read counts
ps_alex   <- subset_taxa(ps_algae, Genus == "Alexandrium")
asv_seqs  <- refseq(ps_alex)
asv_reads <- taxa_sums(ps_alex)

# Load PR2 reference database and filter for Alexandrium reference entries
pr2      <- readDNAStringSet("pr2_v5.1.1_SSU_dada2.fasta.gz")
pr2_alex <- pr2[str_detect(names(pr2), "Alexandrium")]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.2 Pairwise Alignment against PR2 Reference Database
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Align each ASV to PR2 entries to calculate percent identity and extract top matches
alex_aligned <- map_dfr(names(asv_seqs), function(id) {
  # Perform global-local pairwise alignment and calculate percent identity (PID1)
  pids    <- pid(pairwiseAlignment(pr2_alex, asv_seqs[[id]], type = "global-local"), type = "PID1")
  max_pid <- max(pids)
  
  # Extract top-matching reference headers at maximum identity
  top_headers   <- names(pr2_alex)[pids == max_pid]
  clean_headers <- gsub(";\\s*$", "", top_headers)
  top_species   <- unique(str_replace_all(sub(".*[;|]", "", clean_headers), "_", " "))
  
  data.frame(
    OTU             = id,
    `Read number`   = asv_reads[[id]],
    Pct_Identity    = round(max_pid, 2),
    `Top PR2 Match` = paste(top_species[top_species != ""], collapse = " / "),
    check.names     = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

# Recode multi-match complexes (catenella/tamarense) to 'Alexandrium catenella'
alex_aligned <- alex_aligned %>%
  mutate(
    `Top PR2 Match` = if_else(
      grepl("catenella", `Top PR2 Match`, ignore.case = TRUE) & 
        grepl("tamarense", `Top PR2 Match`, ignore.case = TRUE),
      "Alexandrium catenella",
      `Top PR2 Match`
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.3 Filter & Summarize Taxa Abundances
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filter for 100% identity matches and minimum read count threshold (>= 10 reads)
alex_summary <- alex_aligned %>%
  filter(Pct_Identity == 100, `Read number` >= 10) %>%
  group_by(`Top PR2 Match`) %>%
  summarise(
    `Read number` = sum(`Read number`),
    .groups       = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(`Read number`))

# Print summary table to console
print(alex_summary)

# 2. SEASONAL RELATIVE ABUNDANCE ANALYSIS & PLOTTING
# ==============================================================================

# 2.1 Map High-Confidence Categories & Merge with Community Profiles
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

asv_categories <- alex_aligned %>%
  filter(Pct_Identity == 100, `Read number` >= 10) %>%
  mutate(Category = `Top PR2 Match`) %>%
  dplyr::select(OTU, Category)

# Convert community counts to relative abundance (%) and join category mappings
ps_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_algae, function(x) x / sum(x) * 100)

alex_data <- psmelt(ps_rel) %>%
  inner_join(asv_categories, by = "OTU") %>%
```

# Figure 5: Differntial Abundance & Heatmaps Top30 Algae, and HAB Taxa 
```{r Algae: Run Aldex2}
ps_algae_active <- subset_samples(ps_algae, type == "active")

sample_data(ps_algae_active)$month <- factor(
  sample_data(ps_algae_active)$month, 
  levels = c("March", "April", "May", "June", 
             "July", "August", "September", "October")
)

tax_df <- data.frame(tax_table(ps_algae_active), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

clean_taxon_label <- function(genus, species, family, order, class) {
  if (!is.na(species) && species != "" && species != "NA") {
    if (!is.na(genus) && grepl(genus, species, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      return(species)
    } else if (!is.na(genus) && genus != "" && genus != "NA") {
      return(paste(genus, species))
    } else {
      return(species)
    }
  }
  if (!is.na(genus) && genus != "" && genus != "NA") return(paste0(genus, " sp."))
  if (!is.na(family) && family != "" && family != "NA") return(paste0("Fam. ", family))
  if (!is.na(order)  && order != ""  && order != "NA")  return(paste0("Ord. ", order))
  if (!is.na(class)  && class != ""  && class != "NA")  return(paste0("Cls. ", class))
  
  return("Unclassified Algae")
}

lowest_rank <- mapply(
  clean_taxon_label, 
  tax_df$Genus, tax_df$Species, tax_df$Family, tax_df$Order, tax_df$Class
)


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: GLOMERATION & RELAXED FILTERING (PROTECT BLOOM TAXA)
# ==============================================================================

counts_raw <- as(otu_table(ps_algae_active), "matrix")
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_algae_active)) counts_raw <- t(counts_raw)

counts_species <- rowsum(counts_raw, group = lowest_rank)

# Keep taxa present in at least 1 sample with >= 5 total reads
keep_taxa <- rowSums(counts_species > 0) >= 1 & rowSums(counts_species) >= 5
counts_species_filt <- counts_species[keep_taxa, ]

months_vector <- as.character(sample_data(ps_algae_active)$month)


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: RUN ALDEx2 (CLR + KRUSKAL-WALLIS ANOVA)
# ==============================================================================

set.seed(123)
clr_species <- aldex.clr(
  reads = counts_species_filt, 
  conds = months_vector, 
  mc.samples = 128, 
  denom = "all"
)
kw_species_res <- aldex.kw(clr_species, useMC = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 4: CALCULATE MONTHLY CLR MEANS
# ==============================================================================

mc_instances <- clr_species@analysisData

clr_means <- sapply(mc_instances, function(sample_mc) {
  rowMeans(sample_mc)
})
rownames(clr_means) <- rownames(counts_species_filt)

target_months <- c("March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October")

monthly_clr_means <- sapply(target_months, function(m) {
  rowMeans(clr_means[, months_vector == m, drop = FALSE])
})

```

```{r Algae: Month Heatmap Top 30}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. RANK TOP 30 TAXA & SORT BY PEAK MONTH (WATERFALL ORDER)

# Extract significant taxa
sig_taxa <- rownames(kw_species_res)[kw_species_res$kw.eBH < 0.05]
if (length(sig_taxa) == 0) sig_taxa <- rownames(kw_species_res)[kw_species_res$kw.ep < 0.05]
if (length(sig_taxa) < 30) sig_taxa <- rownames(monthly_clr_means)

heatmap_matrix <- monthly_clr_means[sig_taxa, , drop = FALSE]

# Calculate max seasonal amplitude (ΔCLR) and filter top 30
delta_clr <- apply(heatmap_matrix, 1, function(row) max(row) - min(row))
top30_taxa <- names(sort(delta_clr, decreasing = TRUE))[1:min(30, length(delta_clr))]

heatmap_matrix_top30 <- heatmap_matrix[top30_taxa, , drop = FALSE]

# Row Z-score normalization
heatmap_matrix_scaled <- t(scale(t(heatmap_matrix_top30)))
heatmap_matrix_scaled[is.na(heatmap_matrix_scaled)] <- 0

# Sort rows strictly by peak month timing (March -> October)
peak_month_order  <- order(max.col(heatmap_matrix_scaled, ties.method = "first"))
heatmap_waterfall <- heatmap_matrix_scaled[peak_month_order, , drop = FALSE]

# Format row labels: replace underscores with spaces & keep "sp." un-italicized
italic_labels <- as.expression(lapply(rownames(heatmap_waterfall), function(x) {
  x_clean <- gsub("_", " ", x)
  if (grepl(" sp\\.$", x_clean)) {
    base_name <- gsub(" sp\\.$", "", x_clean)
    bquote(italic(.(base_name)) ~ "sp.")
  } else {
    bquote(italic(.(x_clean)))
  }
}))

# ==============================================================================
# 2. RENDER WATERFALL HEATMAP

heatmap_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "#F7F7F7", "#B2182B"))(100)

ph_algae <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  heatmap_waterfall,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,               # Chronological month order
  cluster_rows = FALSE,               # Disables cladogram for strict waterfall
  labels_row   = italic_labels,       # Italicized taxon names (plain "sp.")
  scale        = "none",              # Matrix pre-scaled by Z-score
  color        = heatmap_colors,
  border_color = "grey90",
  cellwidth    = 22,
  cellheight   = 13,
  fontsize_row = 10,
  fontsize_col = 10,
  main         = expression("Top 30 Algae (" * Delta * "CLR)")
)

ggsave("figures/Algae_top30_heatmap.svg", ph_algae, height = 7, width = 7)
```

```{r HAB: Run Aldex2}
# Extract all HAB taxa from the dataset (ps_HAB was made from the already rarefied algal subset)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define Target HAB (Harmful Algal Bloom) Taxa
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
hab_include <- c(
  "Alexandr", "Pseudo-nitz", "Pseudonitz", "Dinophysis", "Heterosigma", 
  "Margalefidinium", "Chaetoceros", "Phaeocystis", "Gonyaul", "Phaeocystal", 
  "Chaetocerotal", "Dinophysial", "Gymnodinial", "Peridinial", "Suessial"
)
hab_pattern <- paste(hab_include, collapse = "|")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Identify and Subset HAB ASVs
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filter taxonomy matrix across all ranks for target HAB keywords
tax_df <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps_clean), "matrix"))
hab_asvs <- tax_df %>%
  filter(if_any(everything(), ~ grepl(hab_pattern, .x, ignore.case = TRUE))) %>%
  rownames()

# Subset rarefied phyloseq object to HAB taxa and remove zero-abundance samples
ps_HAB_unrarefied <- prune_taxa(hab_asvs, ps_clean) %>%
  prune_samples(sample_sums(.) > 0, .)


ps_HAB_unrarefied_active <- subset_samples(ps_HAB_unrarefied, type == "active")

sample_data(ps_HAB_unrarefied_active)$month <- factor(
  sample_data(ps_HAB_unrarefied_active)$month, 
  levels = c("March", "April", "May", "June", 
             "July", "August", "September", "October")
)

tax_df <- data.frame(tax_table(ps_HAB_unrarefied_active), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

clean_taxon_label <- function(genus, species, family, order, class) {
  if (!is.na(species) && species != "" && species != "NA") {
    if (!is.na(genus) && grepl(genus, species, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      return(species)
    } else if (!is.na(genus) && genus != "" && genus != "NA") {
      return(paste(genus, species))
    } else {
      return(species)
    }
  }
  if (!is.na(genus) && genus != "" && genus != "NA") return(paste0(genus, " sp."))
  if (!is.na(family) && family != "" && family != "NA") return(paste0("Fam. ", family))
  if (!is.na(order)  && order != ""  && order != "NA")  return(paste0("Ord. ", order))
  if (!is.na(class)  && class != ""  && class != "NA")  return(paste0("Cls. ", class))
  
  return("Unclassified Algae")
}

lowest_rank <- mapply(
  clean_taxon_label, 
  tax_df$Genus, tax_df$Species, tax_df$Family, tax_df$Order, tax_df$Class
)


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: GLOMERATION & RELAXED FILTERING (PROTECT BLOOM TAXA)
# ==============================================================================

counts_raw <- as(otu_table(ps_HAB_unrarefied_active), "matrix")
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_HAB_unrarefied_active)) counts_raw <- t(counts_raw)

counts_species <- rowsum(counts_raw, group = lowest_rank)

# Keep taxa present in at least 1 sample with >= 5 total reads
keep_taxa <- rowSums(counts_species > 0) >= 1 & rowSums(counts_species) >= 5
counts_species_filt <- counts_species[keep_taxa, ]

months_vector <- as.character(sample_data(ps_HAB_unrarefied_active)$month)


# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: RUN ALDEx2 (CLR + KRUSKAL-WALLIS ANOVA)
# ==============================================================================
set.seed(123)
clr_species <- aldex.clr(
  reads = counts_species_filt, 
  conds = months_vector, 
  mc.samples = 128, 
  denom = "all"
)
kw_species_res <- aldex.kw(clr_species, useMC = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 4: CALCULATE MONTHLY CLR MEANS
# ==============================================================================

mc_instances <- clr_species@analysisData

clr_means <- sapply(mc_instances, function(sample_mc) {
  rowMeans(sample_mc)
})
rownames(clr_means) <- rownames(counts_species_filt)

target_months <- c("March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October")

monthly_clr_means <- sapply(target_months, function(m) {
  rowMeans(clr_means[, months_vector == m, drop = FALSE])
})
```

```{r HAB: Month Heatmap}
# ==============================================================================
# HAB WATERFALL HEATMAP (GENUS/SPECIES ONLY + BOLD RED ALASKA HAB SPECIES)
# Assumes `monthly_clr_means` already exists in environment
# ==============================================================================

hab_taxa <- grep(hab_pattern, rownames(monthly_clr_means), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
hab_taxa <- hab_taxa[!grepl("^(Fam\\.|Ord\\.|Cls\\.|Unclassified)", hab_taxa)]

if (length(hab_taxa) == 0) {
  stop("No Genus/Species level taxa matching HAB roots were found.")
}

heatmap_matrix_hab <- monthly_clr_means[hab_taxa, , drop = FALSE]

# Z-score normalization
heatmap_matrix_scaled <- t(scale(t(heatmap_matrix_hab)))
heatmap_matrix_scaled[is.na(heatmap_matrix_scaled)] <- 0

# Waterfall order by peak month timing (March -> October)
peak_month_order  <- order(max.col(heatmap_matrix_scaled, ties.method = "first"))
heatmap_waterfall <- heatmap_matrix_scaled[peak_month_order, , drop = FALSE]

# Alaska-specific known HAB species list
known_hab_species <- c(
  "Alexandrium catenella", "Alexandrium fundyense", "Alexandrium tamarense",
  "Pseudo-nitzschia australis", "Pseudo-nitzschia multiseries", 
  "Pseudo-nitzschia seriata", "Pseudo-nitzschia pungens", "Pseudo-nitzschia delicatissima",
  "Dinophysis acuminata", "Dinophysis acuta", "Dinophysis norvegica", "Dinophysis fortii",
  "Heterosigma akashiwo", "Margalefidinium polykrikoides",
  "Chaetoceros convolutus", "Chaetoceros concavicornis",
  "Phaeocystis pouchetii"
)

row_names_clean <- gsub("_", " ", rownames(heatmap_waterfall))

# 6. Assign RED color strictly to exact matches in known_hab_species
label_colors <- ifelse(row_names_clean %in% known_hab_species, "red", "black")

# Format labels: BOLD-ITALIC for known HAB species, standard ITALIC for others
italic_labels <- as.expression(lapply(row_names_clean, function(x) {
  is_known <- x %in% known_hab_species
  
  if (grepl(" sp\\.$", x)) {
    base_name <- gsub(" sp\\.$", "", x)
    if (is_known) {
      bquote(bolditalic(.(base_name)) ~ "sp.")
    } else {
      bquote(italic(.(base_name)) ~ "sp.")
    }
  } else {
    if (is_known) {
      bquote(bolditalic(.(x)))
    } else {
      bquote(italic(.(x)))
    }
  }
}))

# 7. Render Waterfall Heatmap with Bold Red Text Injection
heatmap_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "#F7F7F7", "#B2182B"))(100)

ph_hab <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  heatmap_waterfall,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,               # Chronological month order
  cluster_rows = FALSE,               # Disables cladogram for strict waterfall
  labels_row   = italic_labels,       # Formatted taxon expressions
  scale        = "none",              # Pre-scaled by Z-score
  color        = heatmap_colors,
  border_color = "grey90",
  cellwidth    = 22,
  cellheight   = 13,
  fontsize_row = 10,
  fontsize_col = 10,
  main         = expression("Target HAB Taxa (" * Delta * "CLR)"),
  silent       = TRUE
)

# Inject custom text colors into gtable
row_names_idx <- which(ph_hab$gtable$layout$name == "row_names")
ph_hab$gtable$grobs[[row_names_idx]]$gp$col <- label_colors

# Render final plot
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(ph_hab$gtable)

ggsave("figures/HAB_heatmap.svg", ph_hab, height = 8, width = 7)
```

```{r Sampling Method Stats}
# 1. Extract HAB genera directly from ps_HAB
hab_genera <- unique(na.omit(as.character(tax_table(ps_HAB)[, "Genus"])))
hab_genera <- hab_genera[hab_genera != ""]

# 2. Aggregate full algal dataset to Genus level
ps_genus <- tax_glom(ps_algae, taxrank = "Genus", NArm = TRUE)

# 3. Extract count matrix and sampling conditions
counts <- as.matrix(otu_table(ps_genus))
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_genus)) counts <- t(counts)

sample_data(ps_algae)$type <- factor(sample_data(ps_algae)$type, levels = c("active", "passive"))
conditions <- as.character(sample_data(ps_genus)$type)

# 4. Run ALDEx2
aldex_out <- aldex(counts, conditions, mc.samples = 128, test = "t", effect = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)

# 5. Build results table
tax_df <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps_genus), "matrix"))

aldex_algae <- aldex_out %>%
  mutate(ASV_ID = rownames(.)) %>%
  left_join(tax_df %>% mutate(ASV_ID = rownames(.)), by = "ASV_ID") %>%
  mutate(
    Enriched_In = ifelse(effect > 0, "passive", "active"),
    Is_HAB      = Genus %in% hab_genera
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Genus, Class, diff.btw, effect, wi.ep, wi.eBH, we.ep, we.eBH, Enriched_In, Is_HAB) %>%
  arrange(wi.eBH)

# 6. Filter significant results
sig_algae <- aldex_algae %>% filter(wi.eBH < 0.05)
sig_algae

write.csv(sig_algae,"statistics/Algae_Aldex2.csv")
```
